<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par122" />{{GHGmargin-letter|122|s}}
Abstract ideas include also—

(''c'') ''Collectives'' in the fem. form,<ref>Cf. in Greek ἡ ἵππος, ''the cavalry'' (as well as τὸ ἱππικόν), ἡ κάμηλος, Hdt. 1, 80, &c., ''the camel corps''.</ref> generally fem. participles used substantivally, especially as the comprehensive designation of a number of ''persons'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אֹֽרְחָה}} (fem. of ''travelling''), prop. ''the travelling'' (company), i.e. travelling persons (a caravan); {{GHGheb|text=גּוֹלָה}} (fem. of {{GHGheb|text=גֹּלֶה|translate=one going into exile}}) ''the company of exiles'' (also frequently used of those who had returned home again); {{GHGheb|text=יוֹשֶׁ֫בֶת}} (that which inhabits) i.e. ''the population'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=12|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=1|verse=11}} f.; {{GHGheb|text=אֹיֶ֫בֶת}} (prop. that which is hostile) ''the enemy'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=7|verse=8}}, 10 (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=4|verse=6}} f. ''the halting, cast off, driven away'', i.e. ''those who halt'', &c.); {{GHGheb|text=דַּלָּה}} (the abject) ''the poorest sort''; of living beings which are not persons, cf. {{GHGheb|text=חַיָּה}} (that which lives) in the sense of ''cattle, beasts''; {{GHGheb|text=דָּגָה|translate=a shoal of fish}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=26}} (but in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jon|chapter=2|verse=2}} as a {{GHGterm|nomen unitatis|en=name of a unit}}, cf. ''t'', for {{GHGheb|text=דָּג|translate=a fish}}, which in verses 1 and 11 is used as the ''nomen unitatis''). Cf., moreover, {{GHGheb|text=נְבֵלָה|translate=dead body}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=26|verse=19}}, &c. (construed as masculine), for ''a heap of dead bodies''.—On the collective poetic personification of a nation, by means of {{GHGheb|text=בַּת|translate=daughter}}, in {{GHGheb|text=בַּת בָּבֶל}}, {{GHGheb|text=בַּת עַמִּי}} (equivalent to {{GHGheb|text=בְּנֵי עַמִּי}}) ''my countrymen'', see above, ''i''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|122|t}}
(''d'') Conversely the feminine form of substantives is sometimes used (as in Arabic) as a ''nomen unitatis'', i.e. to indicate a ''single'' example of a class which is denoted by the masculine form; cf. {{GHGheb|text=אֳנִי|translate=a fleet}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=9|verse=26}}), {{GHGheb|text=אֳנִיָּה|translate=a}} single ''ship'' ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Jon|chapter=1|verse=3}} ff.); {{GHGheb|text=צַ֫יִד|translate=hunting, game}}, {{GHGheb|text=צֵידָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=3}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}} ({{GHGheb|text=צָ֑יִד}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}) ''a piece of venison''; {{GHGheb|text=שֵׂעָר|translate=hair}} (coll.), {{GHGheb|text=שַֽׂעֲרָה|translate=a}} single ''hair'' ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=20|verse=16}}; in the plural, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=40|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=69|verse=5|hidebook=1}}); {{GHGheb|text=שִׁיר|translate=a poem}}, frequently collective, {{GHGheb|text=שִׁירָה|translate=a}} single ''song''; so probably also {{GHGheb|text=תְּאֵנָה|translate=a fig}} (the corresponding masculine ''tîn'' is collective in Arabic); {{GHGheb|text=שֽׁוֹשַׁנָּה|translate=a lily}} (also {{GHGheb|text=שׁוֹשָׁן}}); {{GHGheb|text=לְבֵנָה|translate=a brick}} (Arab. ''libina'', but ''libin'' collective), &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|122|u}}
(''e'') The feminine is also used for things ''without life'' (as being weaker or less important), which are named from their resemblance to ''organic'' things expressed by the corresponding masculine form; cf. {{GHGheb|text=יָרֵךְ|translate=side}} (of the body), ''thigh'', {{GHGheb|text=יְרֵכָה}} or {{GHGheb|text=יַרְכָּה|translate=back part, border}} (of a country, house, &c.); {{GHGheb|text=מֵ֫צַח|translate=forehead}}, {{GHGheb|text=מִצְחָה|translate=greaves}}. On a similar distinction between the masculine for natural, and the feminine for artificial objects, see {{GHGpar|87|o}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|122|v}}
Rem. The juxtaposition of the masculine and feminine from the same stem serves sometimes to express entirety; e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=3|verse=1}} {{GHGheb|text=מַשְׁעֵן וּמַשְׁעֵנָה|translate=stay and staff}}, i.e. every kind of support (unless we omit verse {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=3|verse=1b|hidebook=completely|fullsizeverse=1}} as a gloss and take ''staff'' as = ''staff-bearer, official''; the list of officials begins in verse 2); cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=16|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=8|verse=13}}. For similar groupings in the case of persons, see {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=43|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=49|verse=22|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=60|verse=4|hidebook=1}} (''sons and daughters''); 49:23, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=2|verse=8}}.
<section end="par122" />
<section begin="par123" />{{GHGpar-heading|123|The Representation of Plural Ideas by Means of Collectives, and by the Repetition of Words}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|123|a}}
Besides the plural endings treated in {{GHGpar|87|a}}–''i'', the language employs other means to express a plurality of living beings or things:

(''a'') Certain words employed exclusively in a collective sense, while the individual members of the class are denoted by special words ({{GHGterm|nomina unitatis}}, but not in the same sense as in {{GHGpar|122|t}}).<section end="par123" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
